reasoning: The claim assumes something the app does not do. Its only source is a secret file that already has a loose mode, set by the user, a backup restore or another tool. No attacker controls that input or this code path. The behaviour it describes is real: AtomicFileWrite.swift:27 calls replaceItemAt, which may keep dest's old metadata. But no default-deploy path gets from there to an exposed secret. (1) config.toml: ConfigLoader.swift:75-80 resets the mode to 0600 on every load() before any rewrite (ConfigLoader.swift:110/189/276), so a loose mode does not survive startup. (2) The DiskCache, UsageHistoryStore, PinStore and OpenAIResetJournal files all sit under directories that Paths.swift:19-22 and :35-38 re-chmod to 0700 on every access (PinStore.swift:27-29 does the same). Other uids cannot traverse those directories, whatever the mode of the files inside. (3) ~/.codex/auth.json is written only by FileCredentialReader.writeBack (FileCredentialReader.swift:74). That runs only when manage_oauth_refresh is on, which defaults to false (CLAUDE.md hard rule, AnthropicConfig/OpenAIConfig). The Codex CLI creates the file at 0600, so the user would have to opt in and also loosen the file by hand. The 'other local user' in the exploit story has no route to cause any of these preconditions. What remains is a hardening and test gap (no test pre-creates a 0644 dest), not a reachable vulnerability.
